content: Melvin-Koushki heads §1.3 with two epigraphs: a couplet from a ghazal by Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī about the shortsighted who paint one man a rebel and another a man of God, and a passage from John Dee's 1604 petition (Bodleian) asking the king to have his servant tried and cleared of a grievous slander. The page draws no connection between Dee and Ibn Turka and asserts no contact; the pairing is the author's own comparison.
refers_to_primary: John Dee, petition to the King, 1604 (Bodleian)
